summary: This informational memo gives application-specific requirements for the Path Computation Element Communication Protocol (PCEP) when used in Wavelength Switched Optical Networks. Lightpath provisioning needs Routing and Wavelength Assignment, and this lists what PCEP must support for it.

eli5.summary: Planning light paths through fiber means picking routes and colors together. This note lists what the route-planning conversation must be able to say to do that.

questions: what is routing and wavelength assignment
subtitle: What PCEP has to be able to say so a path computation server can pick both a route and a wavelength.

tldr.problem: In wavelength switched optical networks, a lightpath needs a wavelength on each link as well as a route, but PCEP had no stated requirements for asking for both.
tldr.mechanism: The memo lists what a PCEP request and reply must carry for combined Routing and Wavelength Assignment: computation type, assignment options, bulk and reoptimization requests, wavelength limits, preferences and signal type.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational requirements document, not a protocol: it defines no messages itself and leaves the solution to a separate document.

sections.title: Wavelengths as a Routing Constraint
sections.content:
A Path Computation Element (PCE) computes paths on behalf of a Path Computation Client (PCC), and the two talk using the Path Computation Element Communication Protocol (PCEP). This memo adds application-specific requirements for Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs), where switching is done selectively based on the wavelength of an optical signal.

A path in a WSON is a lightpath, and it needs a wavelength on each link. In a transparent network, nodes cannot convert wavelengths, so a lightpath must use the same wavelength on every link (the wavelength-continuity constraint). Two lightpaths sharing a fiber link cannot use the same wavelength. Where nodes can convert, the constraint can be relaxed. Wavelength assignment is therefore an extra routing constraint in all lightpath computations.
sections.eli5: Imagine sending colored ribbons down shared tubes. Two ribbons in the same tube must be different colors, so you must pick the tube path and the colors together.

sections.title: RWA Process Architectures
sections.content:
Building on RFC 6163, the memo describes three ways to organize Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA). In the combined process (R&WA), one PCE selects the path and assigns the wavelength as a single process. In routing separate from wavelength assignment (R+WA), one PCE routes and another assigns wavelengths. In routing plus distributed wavelength assignment (R+DWA), a standard path is computed and wavelengths are assigned hop by hop through RSVP-TE signaling.

Only the combined process is the base architecture here. The PCE-to-PCE interaction of R+WA is not addressed, and R+DWA is said to need no new WSON-specific requirements.
sections.eli5: You can have one helper choose the road and the colors together, or two helpers who split the job. This note only covers the one-helper case.

sections.title: Requirements for Requests and Replies
sections.content:
A request MAY include the path computation type: both RWA, or routing only. For an RWA request, the request MUST include the wavelength assignment options, and at a minimum Explicit Label Control or a set of recommended labels for each hop. The response MUST include the assigned wavelengths and which label option was applied. If no path is found, the response MUST say why, for example network disconnected or wavelength not found.

Other requirements cover bulk requests (many simultaneous RWA requests, each answered with a path and wavelength) and reoptimization. A reoptimization request MUST give the current path and wavelength and MAY ask to keep the wavelength, keep the path, or allow both to change. The response MUST give the reoptimized path and wavelengths even if one was to stay unchanged.
sections.eli5: The asker says whether they want just a road or a road plus colors. The answer must give both, or explain what went wrong.

sections.title: Constraints and Preferences
sections.content:
For any RWA request, the PCC MUST be allowed to restrict the wavelengths to use, for example because of the tuning ability of a laser transmitter or a policy. It is not required to provide any range.

A request SHOULD be able to say whether a single continuous wavelength is wanted even when conversion is available. A request MAY state a preference such as random, ascending or descending assignment, and a response SHOULD follow it unless it conflicts with operator policy. A request for two or more paths MUST be able to require the same wavelengths, which helps protection with a single transponder.

The PCC MUST also be allowed to specify the signal type at the endpoints, at least a Modulation Type List and an FEC Type List, and say whether transit modification is acceptable.
sections.eli5: The asker can say which colors are allowed, whether to keep one color all the way, and what kind of signal it is, so the answer fits their equipment.

sections.title: Manageability Considerations
sections.content: A PCEP implementation SHOULD let operators configure the ability to send a WSON RWA request on a PCC, and support for WSON RWA and the maximum number of bulk path requests per request message on a PCE. No new MIB module is defined, and no new liveness, verification or network operation requirements are added beyond those in RFC 5440. If PCE discovery were extended, advertising WSON RWA capability should be considered.
sections.eli5: Operators need switches to turn the feature on and set limits, and nothing else about running the network changes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The requirements do not change the PCEP security model. However, the extra information needed for RWA discloses network capabilities that an operator may want to keep private, so consideration should be given to securing it. Solutions must verify that existing PCEP security mechanisms protect this information and include new mechanisms where necessary.
sections.eli5: Telling the planner about your network reveals secrets, so the message needs to be protected.

Routing furnishes paths to a separate wavelength assignment process
